format: keys/tower/labels/inventory-l29.json: a list; this header is the first element and has no floor, a or b; every other element is one opening with floor 'suite_revit'. Kinds ending in '?' are uncertain kinds; 'optional': true marks entries not to be scored either way.
method: Worked from the geometry only, without any picture: no PNG was opened (neither keys/suite_revit/pictures/ nor any rendering of my own). Read description.md, drawing.json and layer_roles_from_description.json for orientation, the tower inventory / labeller lists, the bank key's part notes (curtain-wall convention only) and tools/score.py for the format and the conventions. Then, with scripts in labels/work_C/ (cache prims.pkl and the DXF through ezdxf): (1) every INSERT (124: 6 door blocks, 18 curtain panels, 42 mullions, 6 columns, 1 Walls 13 block, casework, furniture); (2) every ARC in model space and in the inserts (2,078) with exact centre, radius and angles, the swing-like ones flagged (r 0.28-2 m, sweep 15-125 deg): 20 on A-DOOR / A-DOOR-HDLN are door swings, the other 31 are bed linen (A-GENM), furniture and table rims (I-FURN) and a fridge door (Q-SPCQ); (3) all 200 fill polygons on layer 0, A-WALL, S-COLS and A-GLAZ-CWMG with size, thickness and direction; (4) all 282 A-DOOR / A-DOOR-FRAM line segments clustered by place (27 clusters: every one belongs to a listed door); (5) the wall solid W = union of the wall fills (less two furniture fills, two specks and the shower's 10 mm glass pane) and, from each end of every fill piece at least 40 mm thick, a march along its axis in a band of 60 % of its thickness: skip material that continues the wall, then measure the stretch with no material up to 3.5 m (55 gaps; run again letting the wall continue through other pieces first: 93 in all, 41 of them new; every one judged: openings kept, room interiors, corridor crossings and corner artefacts rejected); the same march listed the wall ends with no material within 3.5 m (open sides); (6) A-WALL and layer-0 lines that do not lie on the fill boundary (walls drawn without fill, lines across openings, glass screens, casework): no wall without fill except the two 10 mm glass screens with their 0.10 m kerb lines; (7) the curtain-wall panes, each marched along its glass line to the A-WALL pieces at both ends; (8) the door, panel and window block definitions, used or not (the suite's doors were exploded: their unused definitions DOOR_SWING_1_SOLID - 800 / - D09, DOOR_SWING_DOUBLE_TYPE 2 - L16_D07, DOOR_SLIDING_CAVITY_1_SOLID - D13, IN_SHOWER DOOR1 and Doors 1 match the exploded doors; no window family, no window layer); (9) a check of every entry: material just beyond both ends (sampled across the wall), no wall fill between them.
conventions: Ends a and b on the wall centre line at the faces of the wall ends (the ends of the wall fills; the 50 mm A-DOOR-FRAM frames stand inside the gap, so the clear width is 0.10 m less: 1.10 vs 1.00 for the pocket doors, 0.80 vs 0.70 for the 0.70 leaves, 1.00 vs 0.90). A door at a corner ends at the face of the cross wall. A door in a glass screen is measured by its leaf (= the gap in the glass). Doors outside the suite (corridor service doors to risers, two unit doors of neighbouring units) are doors in walls of the drawing and are listed. Optional: shower-enclosure doors (the conventions leave out shower screens), the two doors cut by the view crop (width not readable), open sides and recess mouths (passage mouths into open space), and the fixed curtain-wall glazing of the six bays (no opening sash; the bank key made such glazing in a facade gap optional). Not listed: casework, cupboards, wardrobes, furniture, the fixed glass of the screens.
